subsystems.name: Pressure hull and structure
subsystems.role: a cylinder big enough to hold a landscape, held up by its own internal air pressure and by rotation.

subsystems.name: Rotation and attitude control
subsystems.role: spins the habitat to make artificial gravity and keeps it pointed so sunlight enters the right way.

subsystems.name: Sunlight system
subsystems.role: brings natural light inside so crops and people get a normal day–night cycle.

subsystems.name: Atmosphere and life support
subsystems.role: keeps the air breathable and nearly closed, because resupply is impractical.

subsystems.name: Agriculture and biosphere
subsystems.role: grows food and regenerates air and water inside the cylinder.

subsystems.name: Shielding
subsystems.role: stops cosmic rays and micrometeoroids from reaching the inhabitants.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: runs lighting, machinery and industry, and rejects waste heat into vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Close the life-support loop on a small scale
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate a sealed habitat where air, water and most food are recycled indefinitely, first uncrewed and then with a small crew.

buildSteps.title: Test spin gravity on people
buildSteps.detail: Run crews for months on small centrifuges to find the spin rate people can tolerate; the faster the spin, the smaller and cheaper the habitat, but the worse the Coriolis nausea.

buildSteps.title: Fix the mass budget and materials
buildSteps.detail: Work out the shell thickness needed to hold one atmosphere across a kilometre-scale radius, and choose materials accordingly. Mass, not strength, is the hard limit.

buildSteps.title: Build an off-Earth supply chain
buildSteps.detail: Mine and refine metal from near-Earth asteroids or the Moon, because launching billions of tonnes from Earth is not viable.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture structure in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Roll, weld and assemble shell sections in vacuum and microgravity using solar-powered foundries and robotic fabricators.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a small demonstrator
buildSteps.detail: Build a rotating cylinder tens of metres across, spin it up, and prove that bearings, seals and attitude control work over years.

buildSteps.title: Scale up to a crewed habitat
buildSteps.detail: Grow the design to a few hundred metres radius with a closed agricultural system and radiation shielding, and keep people aboard for years.

buildSteps.title: Complete the counter-rotating pair
buildSteps.detail: Add the second cylinder so net angular momentum cancels and the whole assembly can be re-aimed without burning propellant.

buildSteps.title: Fill and commission
buildSteps.detail: Stock soil and species, spin to full gravity, and hand over a closed, self-sufficient settlement.

prerequisites.why: space stations recycle most water and some oxygen today, but no habitat has grown all its own food or run fully sealed for years.

prerequisites.tech: Artificial gravity by rotation for people
prerequisites.why: no human has lived at a sustained partial gravity produced by spin; tolerance limits and long-term health effects are unmeasured.

prerequisites.tech: Off-Earth resource extraction and in-space manufacturing
prerequisites.why: the structural mass cannot come from Earth's gravity well, so mining, refining and fabrication in space must exist first.
large modules can now be launched and docked, but nothing approaching an orbital shipyard yet exists.
outside Earth's magnetosphere, cosmic rays need metres of mass shielding, which competes with the structure's mass budget.

pathway.milestone: orbital stations with recycling life support, plus short-radius centrifuge experiments on crews
pathway.unlocks: data on how much spin people tolerate and how far loops can be closed.

pathway.milestone: uncrewed rotating habitat demonstrators and in-space metal manufacturing
pathway.unlocks: proof that large spinning structures and orbital fabrication are practical.

pathway.milestone: a small crewed habitat at partial gravity with an integrated greenhouse
pathway.unlocks: confidence that a rotating biosphere can support people long-term.

pathway.milestone: lunar or asteroid material supply feeding an orbital construction industry
pathway.unlocks: the sheer tonnage needed for kilometre-scale structures.
permanent, self-sufficient settlement off Earth — the design's original goal.
